PV-01.c01: A bus carries **people, not freight**, so the rules keep riders safe: a safe bus, a clear aisle, no dangerous cargo, and calm loading and unloading.
The **"P" endorsement** is the passenger mark on your CDL, needed to drive a bus or other vehicle built to carry a lot of people.
**ORM-D** (Other Regulated Material – Domestic) is a low-risk HazMat group; the handbook's examples are hair spray and charcoal.
A **standee** is a rider who stands while the bus moves; a **roof hatch** is an emergency exit in the roof.
PV-01.c02: You need a CDL with a **"P" endorsement** for a vehicle designed to carry **more than 10 persons, including the driver**; exactly 10 is not more than 10.
[CA] Passenger vehicles include a **bus**, **farm labor vehicle**, and **general public paratransit vehicle** carrying more than 10 including the driver, whether for hire, profit, or nonprofit.
Skills test taken in a van for **15 persons or less** (counting the driver) → license **restricted** to a 15-passenger-or-less small-size bus.
Pass knowledge tests on **Sections 2 and 4**, plus **Section 5** if the bus has air brakes, then the skills tests for your license class.
A **CLP** holder with P and/or S may not carry passengers other than auditors/inspectors, test examiners, other trainees, and the accompanying CDL holder.
PV-01.c03: Read the last driver's inspection report; sign it **only if** the defects were **certified as repaired** or as not needing repair.
At the DMV vehicle inspection test you may use **only one** memory aid, and it cannot include instructions on how to inspect.
Check service brakes (and air hose couplings if towing), parking brake, steering, lights, reflectors, tires, horn, wipers, mirrors, coupling devices, wheels, and rims.
Front wheels must have **no recapped or regrooved** tires, because a front tire failure makes the bus very hard to steer.
Carry the required **fire extinguishers** and **emergency reflectors**, plus **spare electrical fuses** unless the bus has circuit breakers.
PV-01.c04: **Close** any open emergency exits **and** open access panels (baggage, restroom service, engine) **before driving**.
**Always check the inside**, because people sometimes damage buses left alone; aisles and stairwells must always be **clear**.
Handholds, railings, floor covering, signaling devices (including the **restroom emergency buzzer**), and exit handles must work, and every seat must be **securely fastened**.
Never drive with an emergency exit open; a **red emergency door light** must work and be on **at night** or whenever outside lights are on.
Farm labor vehicles: sharp tools go in a **covered container** and other tools are **secured to the body**; the driver and all passengers wear seat belts.
PV-01.c05: You **may lock some** emergency roof hatches **partly open** for fresh air, but **not as a regular practice**.
An open hatch makes the bus **taller**, so remember the **higher clearance** for low bridges, signs, and branches.
The driver's seat should have a seat belt; **always use it**.
PV-01.c06: Do not let riders leave **carry-on bags in a doorway or the aisle**; nothing in the aisle should be able to trip someone.
Secure baggage and freight so the **driver can move freely**, riders can **get out by any window or door**, and falling or shifting carry-ons can't hurt riders.
PV-01.c07: **Most HazMat cannot be carried on a bus**; do not carry any unless you are sure the rules allow it.
Shippers mark HazMat containers with the material's **name**, **ID number**, and **hazard label**.
There are **9 different** hazard labels, each **4 inches** and **diamond-shaped**; watch for them.
Hazard classes run from **1 (explosives)** to **9 (miscellaneous)**; ORM-D and combustible liquids have no class number.
PV-01.c08: A bus **may** carry small-arms ammunition labeled **ORM-D**, emergency hospital supplies, drugs, and small amounts of other HazMat only if there is no other way to ship them.
**Never** carry Division **2.3** poison gas, liquid **Class 6** poison, tear gas, irritating material, or more than **100 lb** of solid Class 6 poisons.
Never carry explosives (except small-arms ammunition) or labeled radioactive materials in the **space where people ride**.
Allowed HazMat: never over **500 lb total** and never over **100 lb of any one class**.
Riders may not carry on car batteries or gasoline; prescribed **oxygen** in the rider's possession, in a personal-use container, is allowed.
PV-01.c09: No rider may stand **forward of the rear of the driver's seat**.
Buses built for standing need a **2-inch line** on the floor (the **standee line**) or another way to show where riders cannot stand.
All standing riders stay **behind the standee line**, because riders up front block the driver's view and can fall into the driver or windshield.
PV-01.c10: At stops, **announce** the location, the reason for stopping, the next departure time, and the **bus number**.
Remind riders to take their carry-ons, and warn about a **step-down** aisle, ideally **before** the bus fully stops.
**Charter** drivers should not let riders on **until departure time**, to help prevent theft or vandalism.
Make sure riders are safely on before closing the doors; give them time to sit or brace, and **start and stop smoothly**.
PV-01.c11: [CA] **Carrying animals is prohibited** on a bus.
[CA] The only exception: **certified service, guide, or signal dogs** used by passengers with physical disabilities (Civil Code §54.2).
